entry: A laboratory enables dependency scanning, yet alert generation alone does not explain whether the control becomes part of everyday maintenance.
A laboratory enables dependency scanning, yet alert generation alone does not explain whether the control becomes part of everyday maintenance.
The bounded laboratory adoption process, investigated through multiple evidence sources.
How and why did automated dependency scanning become integrated, contested or bypassed within one bounded university software laboratory over a 12-week adoption period?
Triangulation across configuration snapshots, issue records, meeting notes, policy documents and illustrative interviews, including discrepant evidence.
One synthetic laboratory, one 12-week period and one workflow; analytic, not statistical, generalisation.
Within this bounded synthetic case, workflow integration depended on explicit remediation ownership and exception handling more than on alert generation alone.
